title: World Agent Enhancement — Environmental Responses + Event Generation
description: Enhance the worldbuilding agent with BookWorld's World Agent pattern: setting-aware environmental response generation, dynamic event generation for story stimulation, and NPC management. Uses worldview data from TASK-002.
action: Add environmental response generation to src-ts/agents/worldbuilding.ts — generate outcome based on worldview settings and location context when characters interact with environment. Add event generation — produce conflict-rich events from background settings and character actions. Add NPC handling — create temporary agent descriptions for unnamed characters. Integrate with worldview settings from WorldviewExtractor (TASK-002) for setting-aware responses.

criteria: src-ts/narrative/worldview-coherence-validator.ts contains 'worldviewSettings' in constructor or method params
convergence.verification: Import WorldbuildingAgent, call generateEnvironmentalResponse with mock worldview settings and action description, verify response respects worldview constraints. Call generateStimulusEvent with character context, verify event is conflict-rich.
convergence.definition_of_done: Worldbuilding agent generates environment-aware responses that respect worldview settings, produces stimulus events for story progression, and can create temporary NPC descriptions.

files.change: Add async generateEnvironmentalResponse(action: string, locationContext: string, worldviewSettings: WorldviewSetting[]): Promise<string> — uses LLM with worldview settings as context to generate setting-appropriate outcome. Add async generateStimulusEvent(characters: CharacterState[], backgroundSettings: WorldviewSetting[]): Promise<string> — produces conflict-rich event. Add createTempNPC(description: string): string — returns brief NPC persona.
Add constructor parameter or method to accept WorldviewSetting[] for setting-aware validation. Update validate() to check text against worldview rules.

implementation: In src-ts/agents/worldbuilding.ts: add import { WorldviewSetting } from '../narrative/worldview-extractor'. Add async generateEnvironmentalResponse(action: string, locationContext: string, settings: WorldviewSetting[]): Promise<string> — build prompt with action + location + relevant settings (filtered by term match to location/action), call LLM, return response. Add async generateStimulusEvent(characterStates: string[], settings: WorldviewSetting[]): Promise<string> — build prompt requesting a conflict-generating event based on character tensions and world constraints.

In src-ts/agents/worldbuilding.ts: add createTempNPC(npcDescription: string): string — returns a brief persona string (no agent creation, just description text) for temporary characters encountered during simulation.

In src-ts/narrative/worldview-coherence-validator.ts: add optional worldviewSettings: WorldviewSetting[] parameter. When provided, include settings as validation rules — check if text violates any setting constraints (e.g., ordinary characters knowing about magic in Harry Potter world).
Verify: cd src-ts && npx tsc --noEmit passes

commands: cd src-ts && npx vitest run tests/agents/worldbuilding.test.ts tests/narrative/worldview-coherence-validator.test.ts
unit: generateEnvironmentalResponse: returns non-empty string for valid input
generateEnvironmentalResponse: with magic-world settings, response respects magic rules
createTempNPC: returns brief persona string from description
WorldviewCoherenceValidator: with settings, flags worldview violations
success_metrics: All existing worldbuilding tests still pass

reference.pattern: BookWorld World Agent: environmental responses based on worldview settings + event generation for story stimulation
reference.examples: BookWorld paper shows that removing environmental responses significantly hurts Immersion score (ablation study)

rationale.chosen_approach: Extend existing worldbuilding agent rather than create new WorldAgent class
decision_factors: Existing worldbuilding agent already handles world context — add response generation to same class
BookWorld's ablation proves environment responses are critical for immersion
Avoids agent proliferation while adding the key missing capability
rationale.tradeoffs: Larger worldbuilding agent vs dedicated WorldAgent, but simpler dependency graph

risks: LLM-generated responses may occasionally contradict worldview — caching + manual review mitigates
